#====================================================================================================
# START - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

# THIS SECTION CONTAINS CRITICAL TESTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR BOTH AGENTS
# BOTH MAIN_AGENT AND TESTING_AGENT MUST PRESERVE THIS ENTIRE BLOCK

# Communication Protocol:
# If the `testing_agent` is available, main agent should delegate all testing tasks to it.
#
# You have access to a file called `test_result.md`. This file contains the complete testing state
# and history, and is the primary means of communication between main and the testing agent.
#
# Main and testing agents must follow this exact format to maintain testing data. 
# The testing data must be entered in yaml format Below is the data structure:
# 
## user_problem_statement: {problem_statement}
## backend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.py"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## frontend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.js"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## metadata:
##   created_by: "main_agent"
##   version: "1.0"
##   test_sequence: 0
##   run_ui: false
##
## test_plan:
##   current_focus:
##     - "Task name 1"
##     - "Task name 2"
##   stuck_tasks:
##     - "Task name with persistent issues"
##   test_all: false
##   test_priority: "high_first"  # or "sequential" or "stuck_first"
##
## agent_communication:
##     -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##     -message: "Communication message between agents"

# Protocol Guidelines for Main agent
#
# 1. Update Test Result File Before Testing:
#    - Main agent must always update the `test_result.md` file before calling the testing agent
#    - Add implementation details to the status_history
#    - Set `needs_retesting` to true for tasks that need testing
#    - Update the `test_plan` section to guide testing priorities
#    - Add a message to `agent_communication` explaining what you've done
#
# 2. Incorporate User Feedback:
#    - When a user provides feedback that something is or isn't working, add this information to the relevant task's status_history
#    - Update the working status based on user feedback
#    - If a user reports an issue with a task that was marked as working, increment the stuck_count
#    - Whenever user reports issue in the app, if we have testing agent and task_result.md file so find the appropriate task for that and append in status_history of that task to contain the user concern and problem as well 
#
# 3. Track Stuck Tasks:
#    - Monitor which tasks have high stuck_count values or where you are fixing same issue again and again, analyze that when you read task_result.md
#    - For persistent issues, use websearch tool to find solutions
#    - Pay special attention to tasks in the stuck_tasks list
#    - When you fix an issue with a stuck task, don't reset the stuck_count until the testing agent confirms it's working
#
# 4. Provide Context to Testing Agent:
#    - When calling the testing agent, provide clear instructions about:
#      - Which tasks need testing (reference the test_plan)
#      - Any authentication details or configuration needed
#      - Specific test scenarios to focus on
#      - Any known issues or edge cases to verify
#
# 5. Call the testing agent with specific instructions referring to test_result.md
#
# IMPORTANT: Main agent must ALWAYS update test_result.md BEFORE calling the testing agent, as it relies on this file to understand what to test next.

#====================================================================================================
# END - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

# Testing Data - Main Agent and testing sub agent both should log testing data below this section

        comment: "✅ FIX VERIFIED via backend_apikey_fix_test.py. The API-key error-handling fix in /app/backend/app/middlewares/validate-apikey.js is WORKING CORRECTLY. ALL 5 TESTS PASSED (5/5). TEST RESULTS: (1) Login as buyer@nameword.local: 200 with Bearer token ✓. (2) Create API key: POST /api/v1/user/api-keys {name:'retest',expiration:'2027-01-01T00:00:00Z'} returns 201 with data.apiKey in format '<userId>|<key>' ✓. (3) FIX VERIFICATION - Invalid API keys NOW return 400 (NOT 500): (3a) GET /reseller/vps with header 'x-api-key: bogus|bogus' returns 400 with message 'Invalid API key format. Please create an API key first and try again.' (previously returned 500 CastError) ✓. (3b) GET /reseller/vps with header 'x-api-key: notanobjectid|abc' returns 400 with message 'Invalid API key format' (previously returned 500 CastError) ✓. (4) REGRESSION - Valid API key still works: (4a) GET /reseller/vps with valid API key returns 200 ✓. (4b) GET /checkout/orders with valid API key returns 200 ✓. (5) No-auth test: GET /reseller/vps with no headers returns 400 with message 'No API key provided' ✓. CRITICAL FIX CONFIRMED: The middleware now validates API key format (lines 20-26 in validate-apikey.js) BEFORE calling User.findById(userId), which prevents the CastError that was causing 500 errors. The fix checks: (a) If userId or apiKey is missing, (b) If userId is a valid MongoDB ObjectId using mongoose.Types.ObjectId.isValid(userId). If validation fails, it returns 400 with 'Invalid API key format' instead of letting it throw a 500 CastError. Security is maintained (invalid keys are rejected), and error handling is now correct (400 instead of 500). Buyer wallet re-seeded to $50 after testing. NO ISSUES FOUND.   - task: "C3 Async provisioning — checkout returns 201 immediately, background worker provisions, live status poll + failed-item retry"
    implemented: true
    working: true
    file: "/app/backend/app/controllers/checkout/CheckoutController.js, /app/backend/app/models/Order.js, /app/backend/routes/api/checkout.js, /app/backend/app/jobs/provisioningWorker.js"
    stuck_count: 0
    priority: "high"
    needs_retesting: false
    status_history:
      - working: "NA"
        agent: "main"
        comment: "P0 C3. Checkout no longer provisions inside the POST request. NEW BEHAVIOR: POST /api/v1/checkout/orders debits the wallet + burns redeemed points atomically, saves the order with every item status='pending' and order.provisioning='pending', returns 201 immediately, then provisions OFF-REQUEST via setImmediate(processOrder). A safety-net cron (app/jobs/provisioningWorker.js, every 1 min) reclaims any order left in provisioning pending/processing whose lock is null or >5min old. processOrder is idempotent + lock-guarded (atomic findOneAndUpdate claim on provisioning+provisioningLockedAt) so the in-request kick-off and the cron never double-provision. Per-item cash/points are split at creation (cash_charged_usd/points_charged_usd, rounding reconciled on the last item) so items can be refunded/retried independently. On a failed item the worker refunds its committed cash to the wallet + restores its points and sets item.refunded_usd. recomputeOrderFinancials reconciles order.charged_usd/refunded_usd/points_earned (idempotent points delta) and status (paid/partial/failed) at the end. NEW ENDPOINTS: GET /api/v1/checkout/orders/:id/status (lightweight poll; best-effort live provider sync via GET /vps|/rdp/:id and GET /hosting/:user — no-op in dry_run since there are no provider ids; returns {provisioning, settled, status, items:[{idx,type,title,status,live_status,message,provider_id,provider_username,panel_url,server_ip,refunded_usd,attempts,price_usd}], charged_usd, refunded_usd, points_earned, wallet_balance_usd}). POST /api/v1/checkout/orders/:id/items/:idx/retry (ownership-gated; only a 'failed' item; re-debits item.price_usd cash then re-provisions; 402 with shortfall if wallet can't cover; 409 not_retryable if item isn't failed). SETUP: buyer seeded (buyer@nameword.local / Buyer@12345, wallet $50) via `cd /app/backend && node scripts/seed_test_users.js` (idempotent, resets wallet to $50). Login POST /api/v1/auth/login {email,password} -> Bearer token. VERIFY: (1) POST /orders {items:[{type:'domain',domain:'<fresh-random>.com',ns_choice:'cloudflare'}], client_order_id:'<uuidA>'} -> 201 IMMEDIATELY with order.provisioning='pending' and item.status='pending'. (2) POLL GET /orders/:id/status a few times over ~5-15s -> item.status transitions from 'pending' to 'test_mode' (dry_run) and provisioning becomes 'complete' + settled:true. (3) Wallet was debited (POST /quote shows lower balance). (4) IDEMPOTENT: POST /orders again same client_order_id -> idempotent:true, same _id, no second debit (HTTP 200 if already complete, else 202). (5) INSUFFICIENT: order over remaining balance -> 402 insufficient_wallet_balance, wallet unchanged, NO order row. (6) RETRY guard: POST /orders/:id/items/0/retry on a non-failed item -> 409 not_retryable. (7) OWNERSHIP: GET /orders/:id/status and retry on another user's order id -> 404 not_found. IMPORTANT: dry_run means items settle to 'test_mode' (NOT 'failed') and the wallet IS charged (nothing provisioned upstream) — EXPECTED, not a bug. Use FRESH random domains per call to avoid 409. Re-seed buyer wallet to $50 at the end if convenient."
      - working: true
        agent: "testing"
        comment: "TESTED P0 C3 ASYNC PROVISIONING via backend_c3_async_test.py. ALL 8 TESTS PASSED (8/8). Comprehensive testing of the async checkout flow covering all specified scenarios. TEST RESULTS: ✅ TEST 1 (ASYNC CREATE RETURNS IMMEDIATELY): POST /api/v1/checkout/orders with domain item returns 201 in 2.47s (< 5s threshold) with order.provisioning='pending' and items[0].status='pending'. CRITICAL: Order created with pending state and returned immediately without blocking on provisioning. ✅ TEST 2 (STATUS POLL SETTLES): GET /api/v1/checkout/orders/:id/status polled every 2s. After 2 polls (~4s), order settled with provisioning='complete', settled=true, items[0].status='test_mode' (expected in dry_run mode). points_earned=39 (1 pt/$1 on $39 domain), charged_usd=39. Background worker successfully provisioned the item and updated order state. ✅ TEST 3 (WALLET DEBITED): POST /api/v1/checkout/quote shows wallet_balance_usd=$11 (reduced from $50 to $11 after $39 domain purchase). (2) Replay same webhook: Returns 200 with 'already added' message, wallet STILL $10 (NOT $20), STILL exactly 1 transaction. NO double credit. Idempotency blocked by read-check AND DB unique index. (3) Control test: Different payment_id credits correctly ($5 added, wallet now $15). Distinct payments NOT blocked. (4) Index verification: UNIQUE SPARSE index on transactions.idempotencyKey confirmed in MongoDB. This ensures poller credit for same payment_id is blocked by DB. (5) Regression: crypto-topup and getSupportedCurrency endpoints still working correctly. IMPORTANT NOTES: (1) Used fresh throwaway user (idem5a5497a3@nameword.local) for testing, did NOT touch buyer wallet (holds real $60). (2) Backend logs confirm webhook processing: 'PAYMENT_CAPTURED | wallet credited: 10 USD | newBalance: 10' for first credit, and subsequent replays show idempotency checks working. (3) Both credit paths (webhook handleDynoPaymentWebhook + poller creditWalletTopup) use the SAME idempotencyKey format 'dynopay:<payment_id>', ensuring cross-path protection. (4) The UNIQUE SPARSE index on idempotencyKey provides DB-level guarantee that duplicate credits are impossible, even if application-level checks fail. (5) All tests used MongoDB ObjectId for user lookups (not string) to match schema. (6) Test script: /app/backend_idempotency_test.py. NO ISSUES FOUND. Idempotency hardening is FULLY WORKING and production-ready. DynoPay webhook and poller can NEVER double-credit the same payment."

Failed-item refunds now refund cash proportionally + restore the points portion. Order model got points_redeemed/points_discount_usd/points_earned/points_restored fields. (2) redeem_points ABOVE balance or above the order value must CLAMP (points_applied <= min(balance, subtotal/0.02); discount never exceeds subtotal). (3) ORDER WITH POINTS: POST /orders {items:[<fresh domain $39>], redeem_points:500, client_order_id:'<uuid>'} -> 201; order.points_redeemed:500, points_discount_usd:10, charged_usd:29 (39-10), wallet reduced by 29 only; order.points_earned ~= 29 (1 pt/$1 net). (5) redeem_points:0 or omitted behaves exactly like before (full cash charge, still earns points on the full amount). metadata:
  created_by: "main_agent"
  version: "1.0"
  test_sequence: 18
  run_ui: false

test_plan:
  current_focus:
    - "Onboarding soft-gate: signup -> OTP screen (keeps session) + Skip for now + app-wide VerifyEmailBanner"
  stuck_tasks: []
  test_all: false
  test_priority: "high_first"

agent_communication:
  - agent: "main"
    message: "FRONTEND ONBOARDING SOFT-GATE — please FRONTEND-TEST (user approved). Focus task: 'Onboarding soft-gate: signup -> OTP screen (keeps session) + Skip for now + app-wide VerifyEmailBanner'. App runs on the pod preview URL; frontend is Vite DEV (HMR). STEPS: (1) /create-account: register a FRESH unique email (e.g. qa+<rand>@nameword.local) + password 'Test@12345' twice -> MUST land on /otp-code ('Enter your code') while LOGGED IN, and a 'Skip for now' button (data-testid='otp-skip') must be visible. (2) Click 'Skip for now' -> MUST land on /dashboard AND the amber 'Confirm your email address' banner (data-testid='verify-email-banner') MUST be visible at the top with 'Enter code' (verify-banner-enter-code), 'Resend email' (verify-banner-resend) and a dismiss X (verify-banner-dismiss). (3) Click 'Enter code' -> goes to /otp-code. (4) Back on dashboard, click 'Resend email' -> a toast/alert appears (success OR a graceful 'could not send' error — BOTH acceptable; email delivery is a known blocker, do not fail the test on delivery). (5) Click dismiss X -> banner disappears for the session. (6) Log in as demo@nameword.local / Demo@12345 -> the banner MUST NOT appear (already verified). IMPORTANT: this is a soft gate — verification is NOT required to use the app. Preview may rate-limit rapid automated signups (Cloudflare 429) — retry/backoff if you hit it. Do NOT test backend."
  - agent: "main"
    message: "P0 SECURITY FIX (C1) — please TEST BACKEND ONLY. Focus task: 'C1 Ownership-scoping ...'. The reseller 'my X' lists + management actions are now scoped to the signed-in buyer's own orders instead of the provider's account-wide list. SETUP (idempotent): `cd /app/backend && node scripts/seed_c1_test.js` creates two owners each with 1 order (domain+vps+hosting, dry_run/test_mode): c1-owner-a@nameword.local / Owner@12345 (owns c1-owner-a.com) and c1-owner-b@nameword.local / Owner@12345 (owns c1-owner-b.com). Login: POST /api/v1/auth/login {email,password} -> use returned token as Authorization: Bearer. KEY CHECKS: (a) Each owner's GET /reseller/domains|/vps|/hosting returns ONLY their own item(s) (A sees c1-owner-a.com and NOT c1-owner-b.com). Note the 'id' on vps items and 'username' on hosting accounts are refs like '<orderId>:<idx>' in dry_run. (b) CROSS-OWNER = 403: as A, call action/delete/credentials on B's vps id and B's hosting username -> all 403 {error:'forbidden'}. Get B's ids by logging in as B first and reading B's lists. (c) OWN + dry_run = 200 test_mode: as A, POST /reseller/vps/<A_id>/action {action:'reboot'} -> 200 {mode:'dry_run',status:'test_mode'}; GET /reseller/vps/<A_id>/credentials -> 200 (password null). (d) Empty type: A has no RDP, so GET /reseller/rdp -> {rdp:[],count:0} and any rdp action -> 403. (e) Public still open (no auth): GET /reseller/health, /vps/plans?region=EU, /hosting/plans, /domains/search?domain=coolstartup2026.com -> 200. IMPORTANT: dry_run is expected (mode:dry_run); do NOT treat test_mode statuses as bugs. Do NOT test frontend."
